# HECM Wellness: A Boutique Bodywork Practice Built on Long-Term Relationships

![A collection of beautiful massage supplies at HECM Wellness.](https://www.wellnessliving.com/blog/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/HECM-Wellness-is-helping-more-people-than-ever-thanks-to-WellnessLiving-1024x576.jpg)

Last Updated on 9 September, 2026

#### How a Falls Church practitioner who has been building client relationships since 2013 left MassageBook for WellnessLiving — and how her business blossomed.

## A Practice Built One Client at a Time

Some practitioners measure success by how full the schedule is. Esi measures it differently — by how long her clients stay with her. She describes her work as bodywork rather than massage in the conventional sense.

Esi has been running [HECM Wellness](https://hecmwellness.com/), a clinical massage and bodywork practice at 405 N. Washington Street in Falls Church, Virginia, since 2013. Most clients arrive through referral. Many pre-book in packs of four sessions. When she described her clientele, the number that came up was not the active list — it was the woman she had not seen in two years who walked back through the door like no time had passed.

That is the shape of the practice. Small, intentional, relationship-driven, and now expanding.

## What Esi HECM Wellness Offers

The practice runs three clinical days a week — Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday for in-person bodywork, with the remaining days held for virtual nutrition work. Clinical massage sessions run 60, 90, and 120 minutes, including visceral manipulation and craniosacral therapy. Four-session packs at the 60-minute format are reserved for returning clients; the 90-minute session is the entry point for anyone new.

Functional nutrition runs separately: a discovery call, followed by multi-session packages of typically 12 sessions over six months, delivered virtually over Zoom. Energy and intuitive sessions layer in virtually or in person. The longer fertility-massage protocol runs as an eight-session pack that lets clients flex across session lengths within a single bundle.

She also takes paper notes during sessions rather than typing in front of a client. That small choice reflects the same priority: the session is for the client, not the software. The platform has to fit around that, not fight it.

The vision Esi is building toward is a single practice where a client can move between bodywork and nutrition on one membership. A second practitioner is planned specifically to take on the nutrition coaching load as that side of the practice scales.

## Why Esi Left MassageBook for WellnessLiving

Esi [had been on MassageBook](https://www.wellnessliving.com/blog/find-out-why-massagebook-online-scheduling-clients-are-switching-software/) for years and had already decided to leave before she booked a demo. The reasons were specific and practical.

**Reporting was the first gap.** She had been doing her own bookkeeping long enough to know how much friction it adds. She wanted clean numbers: which services were producing revenue, what monthly volume looked like across the year, how to pull data at tax time without rebuilding it from scratch. MassageBook could not give her that. [WellnessLiving’s reporting suite](https://www.wellnessliving.com/features/advanced-reporting/) — sales detail by revenue category, batch reconciliation, projected revenue — gave her the structure to run the practice on real data.

**Package depth was the second gap.** On MassageBook, she had two packs, and that was effectively the ceiling. [WellnessLiving’s purchase-option model](https://www.wellnessliving.com/features/payments/) gave her room to design what she actually wants: a VIP commitment tier that unlocks member pricing, nutrition memberships that include bodywork discounts, and shareable family packs for the mother-daughter clients already on her roster.

**The booking redirect bothered her too.** The MassageBook link sent clients off her site, which affected both the experience and her search visibility. With [WellnessLiving’s embedded booking widget](https://www.wellnessliving.com/features/website-widgets/), the entire purchase flow stays on hecmwellness.com.

She also valued the responsiveness. After a platform she felt had stopped listening, having real support available to answer questions mattered. Esi is candid that she is not a power user. The platform met her where she was.

## How WellnessLiving Fits the Operational Model

Three problems most boutique bodywork practices share shaped how Esi built her WellnessLiving setup: protecting clinical time, separating new clients from returning clients, and keeping the back end clean enough to support tax time and growth.

- [Differentiated booking rules](https://www.wellnessliving.com/features/online-booking/) handle the new-versus-returning distinction automatically. The 90-minute new-client session requires payment at booking. The 60-minute returning-client session is restricted to active pack-holders. No manual gatekeeping required.
- Her four-session 90-minute pack activates on the sale date and expires after six months, with no auto-renewal by default. Clients are not surprised by a recharge. For the fertility-massage protocol, the eight-session pack lets clients flex across 60-, 90-, and 120-minute formats within one bundle.
- [Marketing automations match the practice’s pace.](https://www.wellnessliving.com/features/marketing-suite/) Rather than promotional blasts, Esi uses the automation tools to send post-session emails with supplement recommendations and to nurture new leads who book a discovery call. She edits templates rather than building from scratch.

## What Twelve Years Builds

Esi HECM Wellness has been running since 2013. Twelve years of clients who return through referral, book in advance, and come back after two years like nothing changed. That kind of practice does not happen by accident.

The expansion into functional nutrition is not a pivot. It is an extension of the same philosophy: treat the whole person, across every system that affects how they feel. Bodywork on three clinical days. Nutrition virtually. A second practitioner coming on board to hold the coaching load so Esi can stay focused on the table.

Falls Church now has a practice where a client with fibromyalgia, a connective tissue condition, or chronic pain can receive clinical bodywork and nutritional support from the same place, with a practitioner who has been building toward this model for over a decade. That is what twelve years of relationship-first practice makes possible.
